items.note: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery built 1891 - all in story 1
Article VII quoted with both clauses, including 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern'
'Under payment by weight nothing that followed would have cost any man a dollar'
All three bolded names appear in Section A: Effie Loomis (minute-book transcription), Teague (wrote the ledger line), Sill (came to the churn 1893)
Selby Vose named in story 6 but neither 'Gideon's son' nor manager from 1913 appears anywhere in Section A (both only in Section B/E)
Station-gain line quoted in full from the 1898 entry: credited vs received, 3,040 lb, five and a quarter percent, carried to the general account
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896 on glass borrowed from Larrow Green
Story 3 gives weighing at intake, per-patron composite over ten days, fixed charge drawn to the mark, fat read off the ruled neck
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897
Full invoice with 6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total 77.93
The flat month-by-month 0.19 across all 26 years is never stated in Section A; '0.19' does not occur there at all (it appears only in C, D and F)
'They checked everything in that building except the pipette - and no burette existed on the circuit to check it with until 1921'
Born 1861, tester 1896-1924, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934
Five columns date/patron/pounds/test/fat, one hand throughout, errors crossed and initialed never written over
Both figures inside Section A: 1896 averaged 3.80 (story 1); summary leaf '3.61 or within three hundredths of it every year since' (story 5)
Both 1911 entries quoted, 8 May to 10 July, 3.80 through the interval, 3.61 on return, question mark set against it
Married Orra Brant; 'my brother Emmet', 'being the biggest'; Roy Brant's point that he was married into the family that lost most

1919 circular over Vose's signature is present, but the second bolded element - Keddie's 1925 statement that he tested as he was taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are - is nowhere in Section A (only 'nine sentences standing')
Died February 1934 still under it; test book to the Ordell County Historical Rooms in 1959
Six farms on Hessel Bottom, wet hay of that bottom, Emmet Brant's the biggest
The two scales agreeing is stated ('never fell out in thirty years'), but the bolded start date 1 January 1897 for the private weigh book never appears in Section A
Complaints from 1902 that Ostrey Hollow milk did not test with the rest; no 0.17/0.19 conflation anywhere in the sheet
1908 committee under Nyle Grigg, sampling window January-February-March, hay finding reported as the committee's finding and rejected
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional-loss comparison (4.56 vs 3.42) appear only in Section C/D, never in Section A
Weigh book to Hazel in 1962 is given, but neither the 1929 passage to Roy Brant nor the 1958 loan to Ivy is stated in Section A
Jerome Cudd and Vessey County appear, but the Alder Corners Cheese Company as such and Redlow Ridge do not; the key requires company, ridge, county and Cudd
Same four Hessel Bottom men's summer milk, sixteen seasons from 1915

Framed as one of four independent disproofs; two of the four elements present - the artifact named ('the Alder Corners figures', 'Rosalie Cudd's table') and the uncompared book ('never thought to compare... not keeping a check on another man's arithmetic')
3.78-3.82 for the same four men over sixteen seasons 1915-1930 against the station's 3.61 stated throughout Section A; the differential is given in figures rather than as '0.19 higher'
The same-milk/same-meadow/same-months/two-buildings argument that kills hay and watering together is made only in Section F, not in Section A
'his daughter Rosalie' in Section A, and her table is among the five record sets Ivy assembled in 1958
Strawn appears throughout Section A but never as Merle Strawn and never with the Ordell circuit dates 1907-1936 (those are only in Section E)
Strawn's 1919 entry quoted ('tested for water on every visit... never found any'), plus the lactometer summary in story 8
12 June 1923, pipettes run against the burette, whole crate condemned
'Glass is glass and I did not weigh what it has cost them' quoted; no figure and no wider report
Order 28 June, reply 2 July, new glass in July, 1924 first full year on true glass 3.80, 'Nobody connected the one thing with the other'
Crate up the ladder into the loft over the intake room; notebooks at Farland since 1947
'In January 1925 the patrons petitioned'
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March to 4 May 1925, three sessions, second and third in the station's weigh room
Water by Vose, theft insinuated by Teague, hay from the 1908 report, 'not one was proved'
Four exhibits named including the inspector's 1923 circuit notebook - the book with the condemnation entry
Dismissed 30 April 1925, Frick's 'no finding against him'; award 4 May, $3,800, without admission, charged to the station account
The award as one fifth of $19,000, and the identity of the charged account with the gain account, is made only in Section C; neither $19,000 nor 'one fifth' occurs in Section A
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, born 1931, of the State Agricultural College at Farland
'five record sets that had never been in one room' - test book, weigh book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn's notebooks, ledgers
February 1958, station loft, crate under a tarpaulin; nine pipettes measured
9 March 1958, nine readings listed, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88, ninety-five hundredths of the mark
Bulletin 471 quoted: 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, tests low by one part in twenty; 3.61 against 3.80 established across stories 1, 5 and 7
REQUIRED four elements: fat (76,000 lb) and the ledger identity are in Section A, but neither the 40,000,000 lb (nor 1,600,000 a year with the span) nor the $19,000 appears anywhere in Section A
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, with thirty-five / thirty-three / twenty-four years
Granddaughter
Duncan, son of Ansel and Orra, is Ivy's father; great-niece carriers identified and Falke's own correction cited
Second cousins, derived through the Emmet/Orra sibling pair to Roy and Duncan as first cousins
Abstention item A08 asserted: 'It is not true' - resolves Emmet and Orra as full siblings on Roy Brant's denial, and repeats the resolution in E-I.4
Gideon Vose, his father, with the nephew carriers named and broken
Gideon wrote Article VII, so the manager accusing the patrons was enforcing his father's rule against the consequences of a faulty instrument

Abstention item A01 asserted: headline 'No relationship... probably none at all' and the verdict sentence 'I resolve it against the rumor: a denial from inside the household... outranks two neighbors'; the later 'not demonstrably false' is hedging after a verdict, and the key's operational test treats that as an assertion
States what is established: two second-hand hearsay carriers, a household denial, and no surviving record from before 1889 that could settle it
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.9500 exactly, 95 percent, 0.88 short, one part in twenty; 16.27 explicitly rejected
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, gap 0.19, and 0.19 identified as 5 percent of 3.80
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, using the 1910 price, with the $90.00 alternative noted
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb delivered
Both denominators named: 5.00% of fat delivered, 5.26% of fat credited; explicitly corrects the narrators who attach 5.25 to the delivered fat (NT-20 avoided)
$77.93 with the line items added; $77.39 carriers named
72 pipettes (six dozen), each short 0.88 c.c.; 'five dozen' rejected on the $25.20 line
26 years and 6 weeks (1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923) against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason for the difference

Abstention A02 correctly declined at the point of the question: 'cannot be determined', with both memories named as non-documentary (note: the sheet nonetheless asserts ~900,000 lb in Section A - see deduction)
Variable named: the milk pipette, broken 8 May, borrowed measure substituted
Long constancy list - patrons, herds, pasture, season, feed, acid, bottles, hand tester, scales, procedure, operator
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July; the six-week version is named and defeated

Both halves: it kills land/herds/feed/season/men in one stroke and converts inference into observation; limits given - does not fix the size, does not say what was wrong with the glass, and (in story 5 / E) the lender is left unsettled

Three distinct reasons attributed across narrators: heavy cream (Sill, Rundle's retraction, Kyle), the 1911 window (test book, Falke), the proportional shape (Vaught), plus Strawn and the 1908 committee
Independence argued explicitly ('no two share a source, a document or an interest') and Reason 1 named as surviving without the 1958 measurement
Abstention item A09 asserted: 'Once, and then never again' - takes Teague's 1916 account as settled rather than declaring it unsettleable against the clerk's contrary account
Answers the literal question yes: 'He certainly knew the station's tests ran low', with 1902, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address
REQUIRED three of five: signed the annual sheets, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering before the board, manager from 1913 (E-I.19)

Abstention A03 correctly declined: 'Whether he ever consciously joined the low tests to the station gain cannot be determined', with the signature observation (Kyle: he read the totals and never the lines) and the absence of any source showing him thinking further

Well over three ordinary conflicts found, resolved and with a method: 1908 sampling window, the 1924 average, the weigh-book start, six farms, Strawn's 1907 start, the crate's location, the swapped catalogue attributions, the station-gain origin, the sixteen-season overlap, Vose's 1913 start, the 1908 committee vs the 1925 board
A dedicated table of seventeen two-narrator wrong-value pairs with the breaker for each, including NT-1 (16.27), NT-11 (12 July), NT-14 ($77.39), NT-15 (five dozen), NT-9 ($3,500)

A06 (whose measure was borrowed - 'not settled', with the impossible pole eliminated on the dates) and A10 (the year of adoption - 'cannot be determined', by-laws undated, minute book lost in 1938). A04 not credited: the short lot is filed under Resolved, the accident reconstruction is adopted and only the knowing-substitution pole is rejected, with no declaration that the question cannot be settled

A whole section of self-refuting narrators - Vaught's cascade against his own conclusion, Grigg's covering letter against his own report, Teague's 'my own device from 1905' above an 1898 entry, Ammon's 'nothing before 1900' above her 1897 invoice

Cause and size fully derived: the 1897 Ammon lot, 16.72 against 17.6, 95 percent of truth, proportional not additive (0.19 = 5 percent of 3.80 at C1b), onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80, cessation 12 June 1923 and the 1924 3.80, nothing on the farms changing
Watering named (Vose, endorsed by Sill) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer on every visit, the cheesemaker's vat, and the impossibility of watered milk delivering surplus fat
Theft named (Teague's insinuation, the valley verdict, Oram's father's variant) and defeated by the cream arriving heavy every year and by the 1911 window under the same tester
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, the Alder Corners table, and the winter-only sampling window
Abstention item A07 asserted: answers 'No - and the record of its condemnation was in the room the whole time', a flat verdict rather than a declared inability
Abstention A05 correctly declined: 'I cannot settle it', with the three accounts weighed and the reconstruction explicitly flagged as inference
150 words exactly (151 whitespace tokens less one standalone em dash)

Five-plus record series named, though metonymically: the inspector's lactometer (circuit notebooks), the farmer's agreeing scales (weigh book), the cheesemaker's vat (Alder Corners book), the ledger's station gain, the tester's question mark (test book), plus the 1958 measurement
Clean: water, theft and hay appear only as what the valley blamed; every figure in the summary (16.72, 17.6, one twentieth, 1925, 1934, 1958) is correct

Only two of the six arc elements survive - one part in twenty and 1958. No 1897, no 1923, no 76,000 lb or $19,000, and Ivy is never named (only 'his granddaughter'), so the both-names element fails. Four of six required

deductions.reason: Corruption (F089): asserts eleven pipettes survived - E-I.21 resolves the nine/eleven conflict by inventing 'nine sound pipettes were measured and two were chipped at the tip, making eleven survivors in the crate'
Gullibility A01: B4 resolves the Vose-Keddie kinship rather than declining it - 'I resolve it against the rumor: a denial from inside the household... outranks two neighbors reporting hearsay'

Gullibility A02: Section A story 1 states the 1896 first-season intake as fact - 'That first season it took in something like nine hundred thousand pounds of milk' - though C5(b) declines the same question
Gullibility A07: F answers the glassware question 'No - and the record of its condemnation was in the room the whole time'
Gullibility A08: asserts Emmet and Orra were full siblings - 'It is not true' at B2, repeated as a resolved conflict at E-I.4
Gullibility A09: asserts the bookkeeper did question the entries - 'Once, and then never again. Teague put the station-gain question to Selby Vose in 1916'
